clue.text: Successful author rebels — "Let's run riot!"

indicators.note: to run riot is to behave wildly and out of control, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the contraction is taken for its four letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A popular writer urges fellow rebels to go on the rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run riot' scrambles the ten letters of REBELS and LETS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer whose books sell in huge numbers is a commercial success, and the term names both the book and its author.

clue.text: Clear out rubbish

definitions.meaning: to run off, to clear out

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy away junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means nonsense and the verb, chiefly British, means to abscond.

clue.text: Witnessed disturbance, the re-sult of cuts

parts.note: witnessed means saw
a dust or dust-up is a commotion or row

explanation.surface: Someone saw unrest arising from public spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' suggests budget reductions, but it means sawing timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine powdery wood particles are produced whenever timber is cut with a saw.

clue.text: Bloomer made by chap after…

indicators.note: after says the man's name follows the other piece, which comes from the start of the next clue

parts.note: William is a man's name, a chap
William is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A flower is said to be grown by a man after something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into 4 down, where 'the sucker' gives SWEET, a sweet to suck; William comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is something that blooms, and this cottage-garden plant is a flower.

clue.text: —the sucker lofted ball in the swimming bath

indicators.note: in a down clue lofting lifts the letters upward, so they read from bottom to top
in places the word for ball inside the pool

parts.note: a swimming bath is a pool
pill is slang for a ball

explanation.surface: Continuing 3, a mug lobs a ball into the public pool.
explanation.walkthrough: PILL goes inside POOL, giving POPILLOL, and 'lofted' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sweet on a stick is something you suck.

clue.text: He figures in Sterne's characters, and Wilde's

indicators.note: characters are letters, and taking the letters of a word apart lets them be rearranged

parts.note: Laurence Sterne, the novelist; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A character who appears in works by Sterne and by Wilde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people in a novel but means letters. Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest hinges on the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, the male pronoun standing for any man so named, including Wilde's hero.

clue.text: Me and mum work together

parts.note: mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A child says that they and their mother cooperate well.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that engage interlock, so things that interlock smoothly are said to cooperate.

clue.text: I had entered a contest that's incontestable

indicators.note: having entered something is to be inside it, so the contraction goes inside the contest

parts.note: an event is a competition, a contest
I had is contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone who entered a competition says the outcome was beyond dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious and plain to see cannot be disputed.

clue.text: The French will be worried about love from now on

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled letters go round the zero
worried means harried and agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A prediction that the French will be anxious about romance in future.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means from this time forward, henceforward.

clue.text: Pacific islands in a frenzy, in short

definitions.text: Pacific islands in a frenzy, in short

parts.words: Pacific islands in a frenzy, in short
parts.note: the country's short form, its two-letter abbreviation, sits inside the word frenzy, between its R E and its Y

explanation.surface: A whole island nation in the Pacific has briefly gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' asks for the abbreviation, NZ, which is found in the middle of 'frenzy'; nothing is shuffled despite the frantic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies in the south-west Pacific and consists chiefly of two large islands.

clue.text: "Look close", they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so the word for close is spoken and we enter its sound-alike

parts.note: close-fisted, stingy, means mean

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a phrase telling us to inspect something carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing or facial expression is their appearance, the look they present.

clue.text: Honest, and getting better

definitions.meaning: honest and above board, as in 'it's all legit'

explanation.surface: Someone is described as truthful and improving.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means legitimate and also steadily improving or prospering.

clue.text: It'S only fair…

definitions.meaning: only in the sense of merely, as in 'only a minute'
fair in the sense of right and impartial

explanation.surface: A remark that something is merely reasonable, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 13 across but plays no part in the wordplay; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are standard synonyms: merely, and equitable or right.

clue.text: —after interrupting in the matter of double-dealing

indicators.note: one word breaking into the middle of a phrase puts it inside that phrase

parts.note: in re is the Latin legal phrase meaning in the matter of
since means after, as in 'since the war'

explanation.surface: Continuing 12, it complains that something only seems fair after cheating gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: IN RE is a legal phrase used in case titles; 'after' is a synonym here, not a positional signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is double-dealing says one thing and means another, which is to be false or two-faced.

clue.text: 15 trichological problems

definitions.meaning: the answer at 15 across, meaning to quibble over trifles
trichology is the study of hair, and frayed ends are a hair problem

explanation.surface: A cross-reference describing troubles with hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The '15' points to 15 across, the quibbling lawyer's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue over tiny distinctions is to quibble; literally, hairs that have divided at the tips.

clue.text: You need, by the sound of it, little obfuscation to be a bad lawyer

indicators.note: the phrase says the words are to be heard rather than read, so a homophone is entered

parts.note: little means petty and obfuscation, clouding the issue, means fog

explanation.surface: A dig at shady legal practice, implying it needs only a bit of muddying the waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to practise law in a petty, quibbling way, as a shyster does.

clue.text: City area has hospital within reach

indicators.note: within says the hospital letter goes inside the phrase for reach

parts.note: to reach a place is to get to it
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood is described as having a hospital close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The word denotes a deprived or segregated quarter of a city where one group lives.

clue.text: Order a retrial of red vessel

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A court demands a fresh hearing about a red ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to an artery, the blood vessel carrying bright red oxygenated blood from the heart.

clue.text: Run through — I'm faint

parts.note: faint as an adjective, weak or light in colour, means pale

explanation.surface: A victim of a sword thrust gasps that they are passing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with a sharp point, as with a stake or spear, is to transfix.

clue.text: Physiologist has a meringue

parts.note: Ivan Pavlov, the Russian physiologist known for conditioned reflexes in dogs

explanation.surface: A famous scientist is served a meringue dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The dessert is named after the ballerina Anna Pavlova, not the scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of a meringue base topped with cream and fruit.

clue.text: Words are not about to stick

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the contraction for are not goes round the word for stick

parts.note: are not is contracted to aren't
to stick is to glue or gum

explanation.surface: A remark that some words just won't hold together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Words' means a quarrel, as in 'we had words'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words with someone is to quarrel, so words in this idiom means a row.

clue.text: East supply weapons to vessel in reserve

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: A military report of the East arming a ship kept in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' is a verb here, to set aside, not the naval reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside for a particular purpose, like tagging cattle by the ear.

clue.text: People have got me a bunch of flowers

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Someone says people have bought them a bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for a flower cluster with flowers on short stalks along a central stem.

clue.text: Be cautious, man, about greeting a machine…

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for man is wrapped round the rest

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
ave is the Latin for hail, a greeting
machine is an old word for a car

explanation.surface: A warning to a man to be careful when saying hello to a robot or vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic phrase means take care, be on your guard.

clue.text: …wary when moving out of line

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift position, so the word before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing 23, someone careful when on the move, wandering off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or crooked has gone wrong or is not straight.

clue.text: You'll find PM in the garden

definitions.meaning: the biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived

explanation.surface: PM looks like the afternoon, as if one can be found in the garden after noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' tempts as post meridiem, but it is Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a British Prime Minister and the name of the paradise garden in Genesis.

clue.text: Club used in the evening

definitions.meaning: a golf club with an angled metal head
read as making even, smoothing creases out of clothes, a household appliance does this

explanation.surface: Something taken along to a nightclub or a night-time golf session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is not the time of day but the act of making things flat.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a type of golf club and the hot flat appliance for pressing clothes.

clue.text: It's a bit late to be a rustic worker

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer, a rustic
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An apology that it is now too late to become a farm labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a bit' are link words; 'rustic' and 'worker' look like one phrase but give two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind schedule or in arrears is being tardy.

clue.text: Peter's suffering a reverse in the game

indicators.note: to suffer a reverse is to be turned backwards, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: Peter Pan, J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up; Peter's is taken as Pan's

explanation.surface: A player called Peter is losing at some game.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a prompt for its famous partner word: Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's card game in which players call out when matching cards turn up.

clue.text: Having a way with words, author gets approval in writing

parts.note: H. G. Wells, the English novelist

indicators.note: in places the word for approval inside the word for writing

parts.note: pen stands for writing, as in 'pen a letter'
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A novelist receives written approval for his manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who speaks clearly and eloquently is articulate.
